summary.intent: Research whether macFUSE FSKit backend is a viable drop-in replacement for FUSE-T+SMB on macOS, then capture findings as a structured todo for future evaluation.
summary.outcome: Research completed with a clear verdict (not viable now: macOS 26 floor, immature/broken per public reports, no CI runner support). A detailed spike todo was created via the GSD workflow capturing the full evaluation scope and acceptance criteria.

repo: FUSE-T uses an SMB backend on macOS — the SMB client caches file content above FUSE-T, serves stale reads, and never re-calls FUSE `open` after a remote edit. This is the root cause of the cross-client-sync flake, not a code bug.
`inval_inode` (fuser's FUSE reverse cache-invalidation) is confirmed ignored by FUSE-T's SMB backend — there is no app-level lever to force a cache flush.

Both platforms build with `fuser` feature `libfuse` enabled (not `pure-rust`). Linux uses libfuse3 mount impl via fuse3 pkg; macOS uses libfuse2 mount impl but points pkg-config at FUSE-T's libfuse2-compatible shim via `apps/desktop/src-tauri/pkg-config/fuse.pc`.

macFUSE FSKit backend (new in 5.2.0, Apr 2026) is fully userspace (no kext), native VFS (not SMB/NFS), and would eliminate the stale-read problem — but requires macOS 26 and is currently unusable per rclone forum reports.

FSKit mounts are constrained to /Volumes, but CLI access is unaffected — /Volumes is a normal path. The desktop-e2e mount point is already parameterized in test-cross-client-sync.sh so this is a trivial change.
The vendored `fuser` channel.rs peek/loop-read patch exists solely because FUSE-T speaks over a fragmenting Unix domain socket — this patch is FUSE-T-specific and would not be needed under FSKit.

code.finding: Contains FUSE-T-specific mount options (backend=smb, volname, noappledouble, noapplexattr) that would be replaced in an FSKit migration.
Custom pkg-config file that redirects `fuse` probes to FUSE-T's libfuse2-compatible shim on macOS.
Vendored patch to handle FUSE-T's fragmenting Unix domain socket transport — would be dropped under FSKit which uses a different transport.
Mount point (MP) is already parameterized with default $HOME/CipherBox — trivial to change to /Volumes/CipherBox for FSKit.

fuser declared with `features = ["libfuse"]` and `default-features = false` — libfuse3 mount impl is already used on Linux, which is evidence the fuser libfuse3 glue works and would carry to macOS FSKit.
Same fuser libfuse feature declaration for the desktop crate.

workflow: GSD todo workflow: todos go to .planning/todos/pending/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{slug}.md with YAML frontmatter (created, title, area, files) and Problem/Solution sections. STATE.md Pending Todos section must be updated after every new todo.
Writing a todo file manually then deleting it to re-route through /gsd:capture is wasted motion — invoke the skill directly from the start.
gsd-tools slug generation can truncate mid-word; verify the generated filename and use a clean one if needed.
Todos should be committed on the same branch as related code changes (not a separate docs branch) — planning changes travel with their PR.

friction: Wrote the todo file manually to .planning/todos/pending/ first, then had to delete it and re-run through the GSD /gsd:capture skill — duplicate work caused by not routing through the skill immediately.
gsd-tools `generate-slug` truncated the slug mid-word, requiring manual correction of the output filename.
The GSD init context requires a bash shim resolution block that is extremely verbose and fragile (20+ elif chains) — adds noise to every workflow invocation.
open_items: PR #560 (macOS-optional stopgap for Test 5 cross-client-sync) is open and awaiting merge — blocks Phase 60 staging wipe+redeploy.
Phase 60 staging wipe+redeploy is still pending, gated on #560 merging and CI E2E going green.
macFUSE FSKit backend evaluation is deferred (todo: 2026-06-25-evaluate-macfuse-fskit-backend-replace-fuse-t.md) — revisit when macOS 26 CI runners are available and FSKit backend matures.

macOS UX gap remains: cross-client edits can take >120s to surface in Finder/cat on the desktop FUSE-T mount due to SMB client cache — not a data integrity issue, but a known user-facing limitation until FSKit migration.
Test 7 (folder rename) remains macOS-optional for the same SMB-cache reason — would be re-enabled as part of the FSKit migration.
